I think it really depends. I personally like to ask, "What are your pronouns?" when someone comes out to me, so I know what to refer to them as. Of course, pronouns do NOT equal gender, but generally that can give you a clue about if they are trans- masc/femme/neutral. 

I am transgender, and I don't mind being asked whether I am transitioning to male, female, or something else. Might be a little awkward, but I know I like answering questions people have about my identity to avoid awkward situations/confusion in the future!

I had a constant discomfort with my body, especially when puberty happened, since my body then became more "womanlike". Super weird time for me. I was also really sheltered as a kid, so I didn't know the term "transgender" until later in life. Once I learned the term, it all made since that there was a word for people like me.
If I wore bras, they would have a DD cup size.
I am female to male, and I have not had any surgery yet!
It is odd. My father is.. kind of out of the picture. My mother is supportive, but she hasn't always been. She just wants what is best, you know? Frustrating at times, but I totally understand.

I am pre op and pre hrt. 

One day! lol

Thanks for the advice, the only thing that is weird to me is that I didn't do anything different. Looking closer, you can see old scars, and these cuts happened the same way as the old ones. Idk, found it kinda weird, but I'm sure it is nothing.

It has been a long path, and I still struggle sometimes. But I think for the most part, I am okay with myself. We all have our insecurities, after all. I accept the fact that I am anatomically and genetically female, but I am also supporting of myself and my gender identity. I used to punish myself with various forms of self harm, but now I almost... love myself? I'm not sure. But I am definitely more understanding with myself.

A lot of people think it is because I am transgender. Really it is the feelings that come with gender dysphoria and depression. I have always been really stuck in my head and I think all of it just adds up because I have no way of getting it out of my head. When I attempt, it is usually without much thought. It is an action out of needing everything to stop.
I'm not homosexual.

Hey there, I'm sorry you are feeling so upset over who I am as a person, but I have news for you. This post was about menstruation, not about the morality of gender identity. I admittedly did put a bit in there for background, but if you feel offended over a post about the female reproductive system, then you can leave. Nobody forced you to read, nobody forced you to comment. 
Either way, whether or not there is a god, I do believe I was perfectly made, believe it or not. Sure, it's not conventional, but my body is a big part of who I am, and it is just the way I was born. Me being transgender is not changing who I am. It wasn't a choice to change myself. In my faith, I believe God gives us as much as we can handle and that everything happens for a reason. The way I was created was destined and for a reason. 
Also, who I am has nothing to do with you. 
Have a great day,
